releases.description:
This release introduces the requested **Replace Mode** for archive links.

### New Features
- **Added "Replace" Mode for Archive Links**
  - In addition to the original **Append** mode (which inserts an archived link after the original URL), you can now select **Replace** mode. This keeps your original link label and formatting intact while directly updating the link destination URL to the archived snapshot.
  - Easily switch between `Append` and `Replace` via **Settings → Archive Link Mode**.

### UI & UX Improvements
- **Smart Settings Interface**
  - Selecting `Replace` mode automatically hides append-specific options (such as `Archive Link Text` and `Date Format`), keeping the settings tab clean and uncluttered.
- **Automatic Cleanup of Legacy Appended Links**
  - When archiving in `Replace` mode, any existing adjacent appended archive link previously created for that item is automatically cleaned up upon success.

---
**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/IshizuEitaro/obsidian-wayback-archiver/compare/v3.0.1...v3.1.1

releases.description:
3.0.0 added a new api support and several features — featuring a unified shared queue, contextual editor/file actions, enhanced Vault archival controls, modernized settings UI, secure credential storage, and significant performance optimizations.

---

## Highlights & New Features

### Unified Archiving Queue & Progress UI
- **Shared Archive Queue**: All archive entry points (Ribbon, Editor, File menu, Scoped selection) now route through a centralized queue and progress engine.
- **Real-Time Progress Tracking**: Added a compact progress chip, status bar indicator, and detailed modal with real-time updates.
- **Item Skip & Preflight Counters**: View skipped item counts and manually skip individual items directly from the queue.

### Scoped Context Menus & Selective Archiving
- **Editor, File, URL, & Multi-File Menus**: Added **Normal Archive** and **Force Archive** commands across context menus.
- **Safe URL Archival**: Capture target URLs safely, updating all eligible occurrences across documents in a single capture run.

### Enhanced Vault Archival Safeguards
- **Preflight Scan**: View preflight link counts before initiating full vault archiving.
- **Per-URL Progress & Cancellation**: Track progress per URL with instant cancellation support.
- **Safe Cancellation Behavior**: In-flight HTTP/API results are never written to documents after an archive run is canceled.
- **Status Bar Reopening**: Re-open active/suspended progress modals anytime from the status bar.

### Smart Domain Filtering
- **Hostname Boundary Filtering**: Ignore domain rules now apply cleanly at hostname boundaries while remaining fully compatible with legacy ignore patterns.

---

## Security & Settings Modernization

### Obsidian SecretStorage Support
- **Secure Credentials**: Integrated native Obsidian `SecretStorage` with auto-migration from plaintext credentials.
- **Mode Flexibility**: Choose between `SecretStorage` and plaintext mode without losing existing credentials or settings.

### Searchable Declarative Settings (Obsidian 1.13+)
- **Modern Settings UI**: Searchable settings with inline validation on Obsidian 1.13+.
- **Legacy Compatibility**: Smooth fallback renderer for Obsidian 1.8.10–1.12.

---

## Performance & Reliability Improvements

- **Lazy Scheduler Startup**: Deferred pending queue polling until the Obsidian workspace layout is fully ready.
- **Idle Timer Cleanup**: Polling timers are automatically released when the queue is empty and woke up upon new entries.
- **Production Minification**: Minified production bundle for reduced plugin memory footprint and faster load times.

---

## Full Commit Changelog

For a detailed list of changes, view the [Full Changelog (2.1.1...3.0.0)](https://github.com/IshizuEitaro/obsidian-wayback-archiver/compare/2.1.1...3.0.0).

This update focuses on reliability, compatibility, and safer releases.

## Improvements

 - Improved handling of asynchronous archive commands and background operations.
 - Added clear error notices when archive actions, queue checks, or modal actions fail.
 - Improved pending archive queue recovery so scheduled checks continue after errors.
 - Prevented duplicate substitution-rule removals while settings are being saved.
 - Restored substitution rules automatically when saving a removal fails.
 - Improved compatibility with Obsidian popout windows.
 - Replaced the deprecated builtin-modules dependency with Node’s native module API.
 - Updated the release workflow to use Node.js 24 LTS, frozen dependency installation, and artifact provenance attestations.

 - Added additional automated tests and stricter promise-safety checks.

There are no intentional changes to the plugin’s archive providers or note-format behavior in this release.

# Release Notes - v2.1.0

## Improvements & Bug Fixes
* **Fallback Behavior Fix (Archiver Service)**: Fixed an issue with fallback providers when custom archiving policies are defined. The Archiver Service now properly falls back to using the default Wayback provider if a URL does not match any specified rules in your archiving policies.

## Security & Dependency Updates
* **Vulnerability Fix (`undici`)**: Overrode the `undici` dependency (used internally via `vitest` -> `jsdom`) to `7.28.0` to resolve multiple security advisories (including CVE-2026-6734, CVE-2026-6733, CVE-2026-11525, and CVE-2026-9678) regarding response queue poisoning, same-site cookie downgrades, and cache bypass disclosures.

releases.description:
# Release v2.0.0

This release adds support for alternative archive fallback providers, symmetric command sets for single-note and vault scopes, and queue-based background submission features.

## ⚠️ Important Note regarding Alternative Providers
*   **No Official APIs (Best-Effort Basis):** `archive.today` and `Web Gyotaku` (megalodon.jp) do not offer official, stable developer APIs. Support for these providers is implemented via HTTP request and HTML response parsing.
*   **Instability Risk:** Due to the absence of official structured APIs (like JSON), these integrations rely on parsing raw HTML markup to extract snapshot URLs. Consequently, these features are inherently unstable. Any changes to their website layouts, IP-based rate limiting, or CAPTCHAs can prevent URL extraction at any time. This integration is provided strictly on a **best-effort** basis.

## Added
*   **Alternative Archive Providers (archive.today & Web Gyotaku):** Resolves existing snapshots on alternative sites (`archive.today` and `megalodon.jp`) when Wayback Machine does not contain the target URL.
*   **Per-URL Archive Policies:** Allows defining rules to use specific archive providers based on URL patterns.
*   **Standard & Force-Replace Command Sets:** Added symmetric command configurations for both individual notes and vault-wide scopes:
    *   **Standard Insert:** Checks if an adjacent archive link already exists. If found, does not retrieve or modify the link to prevent overriding.
    *   **Force Replace:** Overwrites existing adjacent archive links with retrieved fallback snapshots.
*   **Experimental `archive.today` Background Submission:** Submits URLs to `archive.today` via HTTP and polls for status asynchronously using a background queue.

releases.description:
The update is about cleaning up toolchain and tackling vulnerabilities. No impact on user experience.

## Security
- Dependency Hardening: Removed other redundant packages to significantly reduce the project's security footprint.
- Vulnerability Remediation: Addressed high/moderate-severity vulnerabilities in transitive dependencies (flatted, picomatch) by enforcing patched versions via pnpm overrides.

## Maintenance & Cleanup
- Major Dependency Audit: Streamlined the project by removing multiple unnecessary packages, including rollup, minimatch, jsdom, eslint-related tools, and @vitest/ui.
- Tooling Updates: Upgraded the core development toolchain—including typescript, vitest, oxlint, and vite—to their latest versions for improved stability and build performance. Oxfmt is too new to update.
- Reliability: Verified all changes through a comprehensive 21-test suite pass, ensuring full compatibility and stability of the plugin's features.
